title: Efficient Graph State Purification with Factorized Graph-Preserving Operations across Local Clifford Orbits
summary: A framework for designing multipartite entanglement purification circuits using graph-preserving Clifford operations and local-complementation orbits.
overview: This work represents a restricted family of Clifford operations as permutations of graph-basis labels. Factoring these operations and organizing them by local-complementation orbits makes it possible to search for purification circuits across related graph states. Numerical studies evaluate finite-size circuits with gate and measurement noise.
scope: The reported advantages concern the graph-state families, noise models, and finite-size circuits studied in the preprint. They do not establish that every graph state or every hardware setting benefits equally.
contributions: Characterized factorized graph-preserving Clifford operations through bipartiteness and leaf structure, obtaining compact homogeneous and bilocal gate families for graph-basis simulation.
Organized gate families across local-complementation orbits using minimum-edge representatives, allowing purification circuits to be transferred between locally Clifford-equivalent graph states.

title: GHZ-Preserving Gates and Optimized Distillation Circuits
summary: Efficient simulation of GHZ-preserving operations enables the search for entanglement distillation circuits tailored to noise.
overview: By restricting attention to operations that preserve the GHZ structure, this work makes circuit simulation efficient enough to support an optimization procedure for entanglement distillation. The construction also applies to graph states related to GHZ states by local Clifford transformations.
scope: The constant-time claim describes the simulation of a gate in the specialized representation. It is not a claim that arbitrary quantum circuits, state preparation, or the entire optimization procedure have constant cost.
abstract: Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states play a central role in quantum computing and communication protocols, as a typical multipartite entanglement resource. This work introduces an efficient enumeration and simulation method for circuits that preserve and distill noisy GHZ states, significantly reducing the simulation complexity of a gate on n qubits, from exponential O(2ⁿ) for standard state-vector methods or O(n) for Clifford circuits, to a constant O(1) for the method presented here. This method has profound implications for the design of quantum networks, where preservation and purification of entanglement with minimal resource overhead is critical. In particular, we demonstrate the use of the new method in an optimization procedure enabled by the fast simulation, that discovers GHZ distillation circuits far outperforming the state of the art. Fine-tuning to arbitrary noise models is possible as well. We also show that the method naturally extends to graph states that are local Clifford equivalent to GHZ states.
contributions: Classified GHZ-preserving local Clifford operations and derived an affine binary representation of their action on GHZ-basis labels, enabling O(1) online label updates.
Used this representation for noisy-circuit search and finite-resource distillation optimization, and implemented the framework in GHZPreserving.jl.

title: Interfacial Charge Transfer and Gate-Induced Hysteresis in Monochalcogenide InSe/GaSe Heterostructures
summary: An experimental study of charge transfer and gate-dependent transport in stacked InSe/GaSe semiconductor layers.
overview: The study examines mechanically assembled InSe/GaSe heterostructures. Transport measurements reveal hysteresis and a time-dependent conductance response to applied gate voltage, interpreted in terms of charge transfer between the two layers.
scope: The observations concern the fabricated InSe/GaSe devices and their measurement conditions. The journal article provides the device preparation, transport measurements, and interpretation.
relatedLabel: Earlier experimental research at Case Western Reserve University

title: Wide Aperture Exoplanet Telescope: a low-cost flat configuration for a 100+ meter ground based telescope
journal: Journal of Astronomical Telescopes, Instruments, and Systems
summary: A telescope design study using an elongated aperture and a low-rise mount to explore the cost and feasibility of large ground-based instruments.
overview: The Wide Aperture Exoplanet Telescope concept combines an asymmetric filled aperture with a beam path designed to simplify the supporting structure. The paper develops the configuration and examines the design considerations and scaling that motivate it.
scope: This is a proposed telescope configuration and design study, not a report of a constructed 100-meter telescope.
relatedLabel: Earlier telescope-design research at Case Western Reserve University
